answer.book: Keckermann's Systema compendiosum totius mathematicae is a volume of several works: front matter (dedicatory epistle, prolegomena, Praecognita, general table), Elementa geometriae, two parts of Scientia optica, Systema astronomicum in two books (the first divided into numbered sections), Systema geographicum in two books, and Commentatio nautica, whose second part is divided into numbered problemata; the chapters (Caput) are numbered within each book.

IV. Problema. An naves velocius ab ortu in occasum, quam ab occasu in ortum ferantur?
V. Problema. Utrum ventus fit aer commotus, an vero diversa quaedam ab aere exhalatio?

VII. Problema. Utrum sciri possit, ex quibus mundi partibus venti spirent, & quotnam sint numero venti?
VIII. Problema. An sint quidam venti stati, qui continuis aliquot mensibus ab una mundi plaga spirent?
IX. Problema. Quomodo pixis nautica fabrefacta fit, & quis fit eius usus?
X. Problema. Quae causa fit, cur vela eorumque antennae quo altius malo affiguntur, eo velocius navim impellant, & cur tam exiguo gubernaculi ligno tanta nauium moles promoveatur?
